newsitem.title: USA: New Horizon Kids Q4 reflects writeoff.
newsitem.headline: New Horizon Kids Q4 reflects writeoff.

text.p: New Horizon Kids Quest Inc, a child care provider, posted a loss for the fourth-quarter in which it recorded a writeoff of assets, primarily for goodwill, of $997,962 or $0.30 a share.

The writeoff related to its New Horizon Child Care centers acquired in 1995. The company also said it wrote off fixed assets of $277,385 for its Kids Quest facility within Eden Prairie Center, where it has recorded losses consistently since its opening in 1994.
As a result of these writeoffs of assets totaling $1.3 million, depreciation and amortization expense for 1997 will be reduced by about $165,000, the company said.
Earnings also were affected by delays in the opening of the Soaring Eagle location, which opened behind schedule.

New Horizon Kids Quest chairman William Dunkley said, "We are disappointed that the marketplace has not more readily accepted our premium child care product at certain of our Boise, Idaho, locations and that we have been unable to achieve profitability at our Eden Prairie Center location."

But Dunkley said the company has made strides at its remaining Idaho locations. "We look forward to improved earnings not only from the Idaho New Horizon Child Care centers, but also from our Kids Quest centers."
In addition, he said the company was pleased with initial operating results from its Kansas City Station location, which opened last month.
Earlier Wednesday, the company reported a fourth-quarter loss of $0.47 a share compared to a year-earlier loss of $0.13 a share. Revenues rose to $2.6 million from $1.5 million.
